760030101.text: #Quick, {NICKNAME}, scooch over a bit and make some room for Paimon...

760030104.text: For some reason, the container seems to already be occupied. It is also clear that the current occupant is most displeased to have uninvited guests...

760030106.text: ...What the— what hole did you all crawl out from!?

760030107.text: Look, isn't that the thief we're looking for?

760030116.text: ...Give it back! Y—You... That's my treasure! Give it back!

760030108.text: Wh—What treasure? We didn't touch anything... We haven't even opened the last chest.

760030109.text: Do you take us for fools? Putting on this "uneven spoils split" act in front of us...

760030110.text: We'll take them all in — both her and her accomplices.

760030111.text: Huh? W—Wait! We don't even know her!

760030113.text: Pick a more convincing lie, would you?

760030115.text: That still makes you a trespasser. And we arrest those too!

subQuests.subQuestName: Enter and explore the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau

760030201.text: After some effort, you convince the Fatui guard to go "take a break" elsewhere...

760032801.text: They're all empty! This is the only one left...

760032802.text: We've looked up and down and haven't seen hide or hair of that thief. Where in the world could she be hiding...?

760032803.text: Maybe she's gotten what she wanted and already made the big escape?

760032804.text: Haha. That's not gonna look good on our monthly reports, let me tell you... or Poruchik Raskolnikov's...

760032805.text: Someone's approaching. Let's hide! Um, <color=#00E1FFFF>that container</color> looks like a good spot...

760030601.text: Looks like a journal. Pretty careless of them to leave it out in the open like this.

760033201.text: Hey! Where do you think you're going?

760033202.text: Oh, you weasel! Trying to ditch us!

760033203.text: S—Say what you want! A true master thief only has her eyes on the treasure. I couldn't care less about anything else!

760030801.text: Phew! Finally, we're safe... at least for now?

760030802.text: Ugh, just our rotten luck! Paimon never would've guessed that the container... y'know, contained a thief the Fatui were chasing!

760030803.text: We wouldn't be in such a mess if it weren't for her. Great, now the chest is gone, and we had to fight the Fatui...

760030804.text: Oh and, and! She even accused us of taking some treasure of hers. Lies! Lies and slander! Ugh, the more Paimon thinks about it—!

760030807.text: Something I swiped in the dark just now.

760030809.text: Is this the treasure she mentioned? Uh, what should we do now?

760030811.text: Yeah... wait no! We don't even know if there is one around here, and, even if there were, it's not like we can just waltz in there, much less her!

760030814.text: Hmm... Paimon wouldn't have cared as much if it were just an item from a chest no one owns...

760030815.text: We should find a way to return it... A—As long as it's returned to its rightful owner, everything will be fine!

760030816.text: But we've probably already caught the attention of the Fatui here, so a little extra caution could save us a lot of trouble!

760030813.text: Mm-hmm, maybe she'll come back and look for it... but will she really?

subQuests.subQuestName: Look for a way to exit the room

760031001.text: Woah, calm down! Things were chaotic back then and we didn't mean to take anything from you. And see? We're here to return it to its rightful owner.

760031002.text: A—Anyway, we'll return it to you right now... Uh, how should we do that?

760031004.text: She probably can't... Maybe we should just leave it here...

760031006.text: ...You can't be serious. What is this cold indifference you're showing to a fair damsel in distress!? If it were Reed Miller, he would have rescued me in a heartbeat.

subQuests.subQuestName: Look for the owner of the lost item

760031101.text: Almost there... I need to make some final preparations. Hmm, "Goldfinch," if you're ready, let's go.

760031022.text: You two...! If it hadn't been you, I'd have snagged the Proof of the Cognoscenti and gotten away by now! And... you also stole my—

subQuests.subQuestName: Find a way to rescue the girl

760030401.text: Nice. Now we can return the stuff we took from you by mistake earlier.

760030402.text: I didn't expect it to go so smoothly... I even got something as powerful as the Moonstriders. I'm sure they'll come in handy later.

760030403.text: Speaking of, you aren't bad at all. Maybe just a bit shy of Reed Miller's level, even though we look the same age... And is that a chatty fae next to you?

760030404.text: #Paimon's not fae! Paimon's Paimon, {NICKNAME}'s companion and guide.

760030405.text: Also, why do you keep comparing us to some thief? We're properly registered adventurers!

760030406.text: Eh? Were you commissioned by the Adventurers' Guild to come here, then? Hmm, so you weren't... Makes sense, she did say she only told me.

760030407.text: Well, this isn't exactly a commission from the Adventurers' Guild... Also, why are you getting so nosy? You haven't even told us your name, that's not fair at all.

760030408.text: Name? Call me Netochka. Soon enough though, I'll be known as the reincarnation of the legendary thief Reed Miller, heir to the Great Treasure — Netochka, the Thief Extraordinaire! Hehe.

760030410.text: Thief Extraordinaire is cool and all, but "Honorary Knight" just has that righteous ring to it. And... it makes Paimon happy to think about the old friends who use this title!

760030415.text: Anyway... You're not here for a commission, and you don't like Reed Miller, so why are you interested in the Proof of the Cognoscenti?

760030416.text: ...Ahh, is this about the Great Treasure? No romance or destiny involved, just here for the loot?

760030412.text: Well, I've heard stories like that, though they sound more like things children would enjoy?

760030414.text: Oh! I get it, you're just trying to act tough. It's fine to be a nobody, as long as you make something of yourself later, like me!

760030301.text: Just lock her up here? Is that what we're doing?

760030304.text: That's "Poruchik Raskolnikov" to you, thief. Show some respect.

760030305.text: Forget about her. Where's the chest? Have you delivered it to the <color=#00E1FFFF>archives</color>?

760030306.text: Oh, Bakunin's on leave today. I bet he's downing another cup at The Flagship right now.

760030307.text: He sure knows how to enjoy life... Let's leave the chest in the <color=#00E1FFFF>dormitory</color> for now and worry about it tomorrow.

760033301.text: Netochka... Are you sure it's this way? It looks dangerous...

760033302.text: Trust me, this is definitely the right way. Besides, isn't sneaking across rooftops what cool rogues do? Ahem... We need to keep our voices down.

760033303.text: Don't worry, Snowy Owl. I'm here with you. Let's go!

760033304.text: (I'll leave the one on the right to you, Goldfinch!)

760033305.text: (Oh, I didn't expect the Moonstriders to come in handy so soon. I'll take care of the top, watch this!)

760033312.text: Piece of cake! Are you all okay?

760033313.text: Paimon didn't expect you to be this good, Netochka...

760033306.text: Of course! How else would I live up to the title of the great Reed Miller, returned to Teyvat at last?

760033307.text: You can count on me from now on, heh heh.

760031801.text: Huh? How did we end up on the other side? We followed the floor plan exactly.

760031802.text: Do ants in a maze know that they travel along pre-designed paths? I am surprised that you took the bait without a speck of doubt.

760031803.text: You've fallen right into my trap, little thief.

760031805.text: It's Poruchik Raskolnikov. It's been a while, Netochka. I never expected Police Chief Stalanov's daughter to end up playing thief in this godforsaken place.

760031807.text: It seems these two playmates in your game of house don't know you very well. Not that it matters.

760031808.text: I must say, your little farce helped me root out quite a few deceptive, two-faced subordinates.

760031809.text: Organization members who fail to execute orders to the letter should be terminated, immediately.

760031810.text: Never mind Netochka's background. We've met lots of odd ducks — so what if she's the police chief's daughter?

760031812.text: And all that talk about executing orders to the letter... You're all just moving a chest back and forth! The one giving nonsensical orders is the real weirdo here.

760031815.text: Oh, right! All this nonsense almost made Paimon forget that — that's what's important here!

760031816.text: And it doesn't belong to the Fatui. I must take it back — that's my mission!

760031817.text: Take it back? Ridiculous. Of course Reed Miller's treasure doesn't belong to the Fatui — it belongs to Her Majesty the Tsaritsa.

760031818.text: Whoever brings the Great Treasure back to Snezhnograd will be rewarded. Should I do so, I could even be promoted to staff officer.

760031819.text: I knew it. You're as obsessed with these titles as ever.

760031820.text: ...Enough! Since you claim to be Reed Miller's successor, you must be prepared to follow in his footsteps too.

760031821.text: This place shall be your execution ground. If you have any last words, now is the time.

760031822.text: But I will not relay them to Chief Stalanov on your behalf. It's best that he never finds out what happened to his precious daughter. I owe my former teacher this much respect.

760031823.text: Precious daughter? Feh. All he ever cares about are his endless cases and "promising juniors" like you!

760031824.text: ...Hah, you're no better. Still as arrogant as ever.

760031825.text: But it matters little, because this will all end shortly.

760033801.text: It's just down here and inside. I'll split off now. Goldfinch, Snowy Owl, don't get lost now!

760033802.text: Netochka scales the walls and roof with the power of the Moonstriders and vanishes from sight...

760033803.text: #Looks like she's having the time of her life... {NICKNAME}, let's hurry and catch up.

760031701.text: Hmm? Paimon can see something from here...

760031702.text: Looks like the disposal workshop. It's on the floor plan too. I guess this is where they get rid of defective products.

760031708.text: Look up, I think I see someone...

760031712.text: "Good work, you've done well. Rest up before the next assignment. Ah, and let's have Nod-Krai Hot Dogs for dinner tonight."

760031716.text: ...Wait. Why did Paimon get so caught up in acting?

760031717.text: Looks like you're both masters of disguise and infiltration, Goldfinch, Snowy Owl. You sure are reliable partners.

760031718.text: However, it would be better if you both were more committed to playing the characters, in terms of speech and mannerisms...

760031719.text: Huh!? What are you, a film director? That's asking way too much!

760031720.text: Huh? This is nothing compared to what's required of ballet performers!

760031721.text: So you watch ballet? Paimon thought you only watched... Wait, that's not the point here!

760031722.text: Anyway, let's put the roleplay aside for now. We can pretty much confirm that the guy called Ras... Ras-whatever, has retrieved the Proof of the Cognoscenti, right?

760031723.text: By the way, why are the Fatui collecting the Proof? Are they also interested in the Great Treasure? ...C—Could they be in the middle of a financial crisis!?

760031714.text: "What's the rush? Are you telling me how to do my job?"

760031715.text: "Hmm, this is indeed what we agreed upon. As for what we brought, if you want to inspect them... come right this way."

subQuests.subQuestName: Look for clues inside the dormitory

760032002.text: Oh! Paimon knows! This is what they call "Turning their own blade unto them"!

760032003.text: ...It seems I've miscalculated. The Proof of the Cognoscenti that you seek is in my hands. If you want it, follow me outside!

760032004.text: I'll be waiting for you at the highest point of the Experimental Design Bureau.

760032005.text: Eh!? He ran away? That... that coward!

760032006.text: Leave it to me! I'll go after him!

760033001.text: (There's clearly no chest on the bed, so maybe under it... Whoa, no chest in sight, and completely spotless, to boot...)

760032901.text: (A container that is just here for some reason.)

760032903.text: (Reminds me of the time Netochka, red as a beet, pushing us out during our previous attempt at hiding inside one...)

760033501.text: It seems the Proof of the Cognoscenti isn't here. At least, the chest containing it isn't.

760033502.text: But look, at least we found a floor plan of this place. Paimon's not sure how useful it'll be, though...

760033504.text: Right? How could they just leave something like this out in the open?

760033507.text: ...But if it's not here, where else could it be? Should I check the archives again? Or...

760033508.text: Haha! Seriously? I've been itching to see him eat crow!

760033509.text: Of course it's real. You know what Poruchik Raskolnikov is like. You think he's going to let someone get away with a fumble like that?

760033510.text: Tell me about it. I had a minor slip-up at work before... It wasn't a big deal, but I got slammed over it.

760033512.text: We can't let them see us. Let's improvise and hide. Gotta look for a good spot...

760033506.text: Oh! Guess it'll go to the highest bidder, then.

760032202.text: He's alone? Paimon thought he ran so fast because he was going to call for reinforcements.

760032208.text: If you want the Proof of the Cognoscenti, you must defeat me first! That is, if you can.

760032206.text: Looking down on us... We'll show him!

760032301.text: Phew... We won. Now, hand the Proof over.

760032303.text: Paimon didn't expect you to admit defeat so easily... And there really weren't any reinforcements!

760032305.text: It sure saves a lot of trouble, but this isn't what usually happens. If this is a trap...

760032308.text: Didn't you say you'd get promoted if you brought the Great Treasure back to Snezhnograd? Why are you giving us the Proof so easily?

760032309.text: When did I ever say that I would be the one to do that? Keeping the Proof at the Design Bureau will bring nothing but trouble.

760032310.text: As long as it stays here, there will be an endless swarm of rats coveting it, trying to infiltrate this supposedly impregnable stronghold, just like you lot.

760032311.text: I am to guard the Design Bureau and ensure its efficient operation. But orders from my superiors must be obeyed.

760032312.text: This already constitutes insubordination, of course... but due to my failings, the Proof of the Cognoscenti that we spent so much manpower to find was ultimately stolen by a petty thief.

760032313.text: Now you can go back to Nasha Town... or wherever you want, to announce your victory.

760032314.text: ...Did you lose to us on purpose?

760032315.text: Losing to an opponent who has deep ties with the Harbingers brings no shame upon me. I'm impressed you managed to find such help...

760032316.text: So you did know about us.

760032317.text: Eh!? I knew that you were exceptionally skilled, Goldfinch, but...

760032318.text: ...Haha! A fool blessed with blind luck. I've always hated your kind...

760032319.text: Forget it. Take the Proof of the Cognoscenti. The Experimental Design Bureau will no longer devote manpower to searching for this accursed thing. We won't meet again.

760032320.text: But if you insist on future unwelcome visitation, I'll show you what I'm really made of.

760032321.text: This curtain call is completely different from what I imagined, even with the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

760032322.text: I need some time to think about all this...

760032307.text: C—Could this be the trigger for an even bigger trap!?

760032401.text: If only he were the big bad governor oppressing the innocent, then I would have... Now, I'm made to look like the unreasonable child...

760032402.text: *sigh* I'm sorry for dragging you into this farce. Say, do you really have connections to the Harbingers? That's... a surprise. If you'd told me earlier...

760032403.text: #We could have been called "{NICKNAME} the Thief Extraordinaire and {M#His}{F#Her} Merry Companions" or "Paimon the Thief Extraordinaire and Her Merry Companions"... or something similar? Haha...

760032404.text: Right, speaking of which, you should take the Proof of the Cognoscenti. Yes, it's much better in your hands than mine.

760032405.text: Why do you sound so defeated all of a sudden?

760032406.text: Yeah, why are you giving up already? And, didn't something like this happen just a moment ago?

760032407.text: You and that Ras-whatever guy, you talk in circles around each other and act like everything's settled afterwards.

760032408.text: And that makes Paimon feel kinda uneasy, even if we did get the Proof! It's like a sneeze that just won't come out...

760032409.text: I just... suddenly realized that, compared to Raskolnikov and all of you, I'm just an insignificant character in the story, like I've always been...

760032410.text: I wish I could become Reed Miller, a true protagonist with an adventure to call my own — someone who can claim the spotlight and receive the adoration of all...

760032411.text: So I told myself that it was my destiny to become Reed Miller's successor. To turn my fantasy into reality, I came here in search of clues about the Great Treasure.

760032412.text: Back in Nasha Town, Hidimbi gave me some clues on the Proof of the Cognoscenti and said I was special, that she had chosen me. I was so happy at the time...

760032413.text: But now that I think about it, how could I possibly have been the only one? She must have had other motives.

760032414.text: All that talk about being Reed Miller's successor, about destiny and mission... they were never meant for me. I'm still just a pebble by the roadside, worthless and unnoticed...

760032416.text: Yeah, how does that saying go... "Everyone's the protagonist of their own story"?

760032417.text: So what's wrong with us being "Netochka the Thief Extraordinaire and Her Merry Companions" in your story?

760032418.text: Ah, but like we agreed, Snowy Owl is the character who embodies wisdom and beauty, and who's just the slightest bit mysterious! It's a role made for Paimon, hehe.

760032419.text: #As for {NICKNAME}... Sorry, Goldfinch, {M#he}{F#she} can be the {M#handsome}{F#beautiful} and cool character!

760032422.text: I envy you, Paimon... I wish I could think that way. Do you have any tips on finding happiness?

760032423.text: #Hmm... Well, Paimon's happy just being with {NICKNAME}.

760032424.text: #Whether it's eating Chicken-Mushroom Skewers in the wild or feasting in a fancy restaurant, it's all good as long as it's done with {NICKNAME}!

760032425.text: #So if I want to be happy like you, Paimon, I'd need a companion like {NICKNAME}...

760032426.text: Hmm... That doesn't sound right. Why do you always have to imitate others, Netochka?

760032427.text: You just have to be yourself. Everyone has a chance of becoming Reed Miller's successor, but only you can be you.

760032428.text: But if I'm just being myself... would I actually deserve it? To be a brilliant character in people's eyes, or a special someone?

760032429.text: Hey, why are you still going on about this? It doesn't matter what others think!

760032430.text: Paimon doesn't get why you keep worrying over it. Even if you're not someone's "special someone" or a big name, you can still be happy!

760032431.text: So you think none of that matters... That's really broad-minded, Paimon...

760032432.text: ...Broad-minded? Hmm, yeah, that's right! That's the secret to happiness! Hehe, Paimon can drop insightful lines too.

760032433.text: #Well, since you think none of that matters, then... {NICKNAME}, would you become my best companion? I don't expect to be your special someone, but...

760032434.text: W—Wait a minute! B—Best companion? That won't do!

760032436.text: Haha, you talk the talk but can't walk the walk, Paimon!

760032437.text: Hmm? Netochka, you... Are you making fun of Paimon!?

760032438.text: Since you're already feeling well enough to joke around... Hmph, and here Paimon was, just a bit, a tiiiny bit, worried about you.

760032439.text: Quick, say thank you to Paimon.

760032440.text: #Mm! Thank you, Paimon, and thank you too, {NICKNAME}. Snowy Owl, Goldfinch, you're both my dear companions!

760032441.text: By the way, what are your plans after this? And, the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

760032442.text: I'll let you take the Proof this time. You've earned it. But if we cross paths elsewhere in the future, don't expect any mercy from me, alright?

760032443.text: Oh? So we'll be rivals next time we meet? Hehe, the two of us are formidable rivals to have, y'know!

760032444.text: It's a shame we can't become best companions, but I'll work hard to become your greatest rival instead. Just you wait and see!

760032421.text: Paimon doesn't get it. Rather than thinking about things like fate or destiny... isn't it better to live happily?

subQuests.subQuestName: Look for clues in the archives

760034201.text: (It won't budge at all. Looks like there's no way to open it...)

760034202.text: Not sure if there's another way out. Let's keep looking.

subQuests.subQuestName: Find a way to open the gate

760033702.text: ...There we go! Goldfinch, the hammer is yours! Smash that big guy into pieces!

subQuests.subQuestName: Use the destruction module to defeat opponents
Use the destruction module to reach the upper floor
Go to the second floor of the disposal workshop

760033901.text: Sorry, I made trouble for you again...

760033902.text: We're used to it at this point. Now, if you ditched us or tried to shoo us off at this point... Now that would make us mad!

760033903.text: ...Okay. Then, thank you, for keeping me company.

760033904.text: That's more like it! Speaking of, didn't that Ras guy say he'd meet us at the highest point? Why's the lift malfunctioning, then?

760033905.text: What should we do? Do we try to fix it?

760033907.text: I doubt it's that easy to fix!

760033910.text: Th—That scared Paimon! She thought it'd hit her for sure...

760033911.text: Oh! I've heard about this strange lightning before. A treasure hunter I met told me that, with the Moonstriders, it should be easy to jump from where the lightning strikes to the top level.

760033912.text: I guess you can fly up, Snowy Owl, but what about you, Goldfinch...?

760033914.text: #Yeah! This is child's play for {M#him}{F#her}, but you might have to wait a bit.

760033909.text: Um... I don't think they'll manage that far up. If we had some other help, though...

subQuests.subQuestName: Find a way to enter an empowered state
Move the cleaning bot to a suitable location

760033601.text: I'm ready to go whenever you are.

760030701.text: Everything should be fine now, let's go!

760030702.text: Then I'll be off! Don't fall too far behind!

760033401.text: If only he were the big bad governor oppressing the innocent, then I would have... Now, I'm made to look like the unreasonable child...

760033445.text: A wanted list? I had no idea... The Flagship always felt sketchy, so I've never been inside. This is news to me...

760033439.text: Quick, say thank you to Paimon.

760033440.text: #Mm! Thank you, Paimon, and thank you too, {NICKNAME}. Snowy Owl, Goldfinch, you're both my dear companions!

760033441.text: By the way, what are your plans after this? And, the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

760033442.text: I'll let you take the Proof this time. You've earned it. But if we cross paths elsewhere in the future, don't expect any mercy from me, alright?

760033443.text: Oh? So we'll be rivals next time we meet? Hehe, the two of us are formidable rivals to have, y'know!

760033444.text: It's a shame we can't become best companions, but I'll work hard to become your greatest rival instead. Just you wait and see!

760033421.text: Paimon doesn't get it. Rather than thinking about things like fate or destiny... isn't it better to live happily?

760030501.text: There's nothing here — but how... Did you find anything on your end?

760030901.text: Sorry, I made trouble for you again...

760030902.text: We're used to it at this point. Now, if you ditched us or tried to shoo us off at this point... Now that would make us mad!

760030903.text: ...Okay. Then, thank you, for keeping me company.

760030904.text: That's more like it! Speaking of, didn't that Ras guy say he'd meet us at the highest point? Why's the lift malfunctioning, then?

760030905.text: What should we do? Do we try to fix it?

760030907.text: I doubt it's that easy to fix!

760030910.text: Th—That scared Paimon! She thought it'd hit her for sure...

760030912.text: Oh! True, we did something similar when we collected data for Fanngel. But, what about Netochka...?

760030913.text: Hm? You knew about this strange lightning, too? A treasure hunter I met told me that jumping from where the lightning strikes to the top level should be a cinch with the Moonstriders.

760030915.text: I need to do some prep first...

760030909.text: Um... I don't think they'll manage that far up. If we had some other help, though...

760031401.text: (The section about the Nothing Passage seems quite intriguing...)

760031607.text: Say, the good ol' Poruchik collecting the <color=#00E1FFFF>Proof of the Cognoscenti</color>... Think that counts as an abuse of power for personal gain? I mean, we're here on a mission. The heck are we doing, digging holes for him like moles...

760031606.text: What happens up there is none of our business.

760031602.text: Do you think reporting it to the higher-ups will do anything?

760031605.text: 'Cause it seems to me that they don't like <color=#00E1FFFF>Poruchik Raskolnikov</color> up there either. Maybe my report's just the opportunity they'll need!

760031604.text: You should keep these words to yourself.

760031603.text: Huh? What, are you trying to get ahead of me? That's low of you, real low!

760031901.text: Never mind that now, let's find a place to hide before we get caught!

760034101.text: I don't know where the other card is... but even if you find it, there's still the problem of <color=#00E1FFFF>getting it inside and placing it high up</color> to remove the barrier.

760034102.text: It boggles my mind why the Fatui would invent such a strange device...
